title: Token provenance + adaptive shedding instrumentation and dashboard buildout
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Provide fine-grained, provenance-aware token-level telemetry and a companion dashboard that lets SREs and runtime engineers reason about multi-region failover, circuit-breaker decisions, and adaptive load-shedding. This ticket covers the instrumentation schema, ingestion pipeline changes, metric derivations, and a set of dashboard panels + runbook links.

Background: Current token-level SLIs conflate cold-cache and warm-cache paths and do not surface decision provenance when a request is routed/fallbacked across regions or when an admit controller causes early exit. This makes it hard to:
- diagnose whether p99 regressions are due to model latency vs KV/cache misses vs routing/fallbacks;
- tune circuit hysteresis and probabilistic load-shed thresholds;
- create SLO-aware synthetic traces that represent real customer mixes.

Scope & Acceptance Criteria (must):
1) Instrumentation schema: emit a single per-request telemetry envelope that contains: request_id, token_indexed timing array (emit as compressed histogram/decile string), cache_state (WARM|COLD|MISS|HIT), model_variant, region_in, region_served, route_decision (primary|fallback|degraded), admit_reason (normal|shed|early_exit), circuit_state_at_request (open|closed|throttled), and provenance_id linking to routing decision. Field names must match catalog: redwood.telemetry.request_id, redwood.telemetry.token_lat_bins, redwood.telemetry.kv_cache_status, redwood.telemetry.model_variant, redwood.telemetry.region_in, redwood.telemetry.region_served, redwood.telemetry.route_decision, redwood.telemetry.admit_reason, redwood.telemetry.circuit_state, redwood.telemetry.provenance_id.
2) Derivations: create Prometheus/TSDB-friendly metrics derived from envelopes: token_p50_ms_query, token_p95_ms_query, token_p99_ms_query (labels: model_variant, region_served, cache_state), token_kv_hit_rate, regional_request_fallback_rate, admit_shed_ratio (labels: priority_tier).
3) Dashboard panels: an overview with golden signals at token granularity (p50/p95/p99 + error rate + saturation); a provenance explorer that shows waterfall from region_in -> decision -> region_served -> KV-hit; circuit state timeline correlated with p99 spikes; synthetic trace comparison panel (synthetic vs real). Panels must support selecting time ranges and filtering by model_variant and priority_tier.
4) Runbook & Playbook: add a short runbook section with decision thresholds for rolling back model variants, increasing admit thresholds, and performing region failovers. Include link to canary runbook and pager routing.
5) Backfill & rollout: confirm backfill plan to derive historical p95/p99 for last 30 days and a staged rollout on canary clusters for 48 hours before org-wide deployment.

Out of scope: changing the admit controller algorithm itself (separate ticket), UX redesign of Console panels (only dashboard panels & queries).

Implementation notes:
- Use compressed decile strings for per-request token timing to avoid high cardinality while preserving tail shape for decode-time attribution. Example encoding: "d:10:23,45,87,...".
- Emit provenance_id at the moment of routing decision so downstream consumers can join traces and attribute fallbacks.
- For high-throughput services, sample 1% full token histograms and emit lightweight aggregations for the rest (p50/p95/p99 shards). Sampling config feature flag behind runtime flag telemetry.token_provenance_sampling.
- Leverage existing metrics pipeline (kafka -> metrics-processor -> tsdb) and add a metrics-processor step that expands compressed deciles into deterministic histograms for aggregation.

Acceptance tests:
- Unit tests for encoding/decoding compressed decile strings.
- Integration test that asserts derived p99 aligns within 5% of full-scan baseline on a synthetic workload with mixed cache states.
- Dashboard smoke test: panels return non-empty series on canary cluster after 48 hour rollout.

Deliverables:
- Telemetry schema PR and docs in Confluence (link in attachments).
- Metrics-processor PR + perf benchmark.
- Grafana dashboard JSON + export.
- Runbook entry and playbook snippets.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket. Initial spec drafted after on-call postmortem where we observed p99 regressions during regional failover. Attached example encoded decile format.

2025-02-15 - Marco Liu: Spiked encoding/decoding prototype in metrics-processor. Prototype shows 20% CPU overhead at 1% full-sample rate. Shared perf numbers in PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1247.
2025-02-18 - Design review (SRE): Recommend adding 'admit_reason' label to distinguish early exits driven by policy vs resource exhaustion. Updated spec accordingly.

2025-02-21 - Marco Liu: Added derivation rules for token_p95 and token_kv_hit_rate. Draft dashboard panels uploaded to Grafana: dashboard UID rf-token-provenance-2025. Link: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/rf-token-provenance-2025
2025-02-24 - Security: Reviewed schema for sensitive fields. Confirmed no PII in telemetry. KMS usage required for provenance correlation tokens. Marked security_review_required: true.

2025-02-26 - QA: End-to-end integration test failing intermittently when sampling rate toggled. Root cause: race in sampling flag propagation. Created follow-up ENG-981245 to fix flag sync. QA blocked until fix.
2025-03-01 - Marco Liu: Fixed flag propagation and re-ran integration tests. p99 alignment within 3.8% on synthetic workload. Ready for canary rollout on runtime-canary-3 cluster.
2025-03-01 - PM sync (Ravi Mehta): Approved canary plan. Request to include a short dashboard widget showing customer-impacting traffic fraction during canary. Added to acceptance criteria.
